record.headline: Splunk replaced its three Observability Cloud tiers with a la carte product prices and Free, Essentials ($95) and Premier ($150) per-host editions, advertising bundle savings up to 31%.
record.who: Observability Cloud buyers choosing a plan; the page does not say how existing contracts move.
record.read: Splunk is moving from capability tiers to editions that bundle AI features and offer a discount versus buying products one by one. Whether the new editions cost more or less depends on which products a customer was using.
record.caveat: Edition prices are per host as shown on the page; the old and new structures are not like-for-like, so no single percentage change applies.

record.headline: Slack changed the Enterprise+ Slackbot claim from 'Unlimited' to 'no weekly message limits' with usage guidelines and advanced-feature limits, and blanked the Usage limits cell in the comparison table.
rows: Slackbot with no weekly message limits
record.who: Enterprise+ customers using Slackbot; whether existing customers are affected is not stated.
record.read: Slack appears to be reserving the right to throttle heavy Slackbot use even on its top plan, after capping Slackbot on lower plans a week earlier. The weekly message limit itself is still described as absent, so the practical effect depends on the guidelines.
record.caveat: The guidelines and advanced-feature limits are not quantified on the page, so the size of the tightening is unknown.
